subproblem.title: The constant 2-covector a♭ ∧ e♭
subproblem.statement: For P ∈ ℕ and a, e ∈ ℝ^P there is a continuous alternating 2-form β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2) (= ℝ^P [⋀^Fin 2]→L[ℝ] ℝ) with β(v) = ⟨a, v₀⟩⟨e, v₁⟩ − ⟨a, v₁⟩⟨e, v₀⟩ for every v : Fin 2 → ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a e : Euclid P), ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) 2, ∀ v : Fin 2 → Euclid P, β v = inner ℝ a (v 0) * inner ℝ e (v 1) - inner ℝ a (v 1) * inner ℝ e (v 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. For v : Fin 2 → ℝ^P put f(v) := ⟨a, v 0⟩⟨e, v 1⟩ − ⟨a, v 1⟩⟨e, v 0⟩.
2. (Multilinear.) Fix i ∈ Fin 2 = {0, 1} and the other entry. Each of the two products in f contains exactly one factor depending on v i, namely ⟨a, v i⟩ or ⟨e, v i⟩, which is linear in v i (linearity of the inner product in its second argument). Hence replacing v i by x + y (resp. c•x) turns f into the sum of the two values (resp. c times the value); this is checked by the two cases i = 0, i = 1 and ring normalization.
3. (Alternating.) If v i = v j with i ≠ j, then {i, j} = {0, 1}, so v 0 = v 1 =: u and f(v) = ⟨a, u⟩⟨e, u⟩ − ⟨a, u⟩⟨e, u⟩ = 0. So f is an alternating map ℝ^P [⋀^Fin 2]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
4. (Bound.) By the triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz, |f(v)| ≤ |⟨a, v 0⟩||⟨e, v 1⟩| + |⟨a, v 1⟩||⟨e, v 0⟩| ≤ 2|a||e|·|v 0||v 1| = (2|a||e|)·∏_i |v i|.
5. Hence β := AlternatingMap.mkContinuous f (2|a||e|) (step 4) is a continuous alternating map, i.e. β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2), and β(v) = f(v) for all v (coe_mkContinuous), which is the required formula. ∎
proof_key_steps: f(v) = ⟨a, v₀⟩⟨e, v₁⟩ − ⟨a, v₁⟩⟨e, v₀⟩ is linear in each entry.
f vanishes when v₀ = v₁, so f is an alternating map.
|f(v)| ≤ 2|a||e||v₀||v₁|, so AlternatingMap.mkContinuous yields β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2) agreeing with f.

audit.reason: The explicit determinant formula is multilinear and alternating, with the stated product-norm bound. AlternatingMap.mkContinuous therefore constructs the required covector with exactly the prescribed evaluation formula. No additional hypotheses or circular construction are used.
